svg.aria-label: Duration.ofDays(1) versus Period.ofDays(1) for a QuizStakes bonus granted at local 23:00 on 2026-03-28 in Europe/London, the night before the spring-forward, expiring in 1 day. Shared grant: 2026-03-28T23:00Z[Europe/London], offset Z because the spring transition is not until 2026-03-29T01:00Z, instant 2026-03-28T23:00:00Z. Left half, Duration.ofDays(1), time-based and exactly 24 hours: grant.plus(Duration.ofDays(1)) equals 2026-03-30T00:00+01:00[Europe/London], instant 2026-03-29T23:00:00Z, local time landed on 00:00 on 2026-03-30; grant.plusHours(24) gives the identical result. Right half, Period.ofDays(1), date-based and one calendar day: grant.plus(Period.ofDays(1)) equals 2026-03-29T23:00+01:00[Europe/London], instant 2026-03-29T22:00:00Z, local time landed on 23:00 on 2026-03-29, the same wall-clock time one calendar day later; grant.plusDays(1) gives the identical result. A highlighted panel states the divergence: Duration.between(periodResult.toInstant(), durationResult.toInstant()) equals PT1H, shown in red, because Duration preserved elapsed time and shifted the wall clock while Period preserved the wall clock and shifted elapsed time. An annotation panel states the QuizStakes stakes: the bonus expiry rule is 30 days from grant, and whether that means 30 times 24 hours (Duration) or 30 calendar days (Period) is a business decision, not an implementation detail — across a DST boundary the two answers differ by an hour, enough to expire a bonus a client believed was still live, reversing it to PROMOTIONAL_EXPENSE.
svg.text: Scenario: a QuizStakes bonus granted at local 23:00 on 2026-03-28 in Europe/London — the night before the spring-forward — expiring "in 1 day".
offset Z (GMT) — spring transition not until 2026-03-29T01:00Z
local time landed on: 23:00 on 2026-03-29 (same wall clock)
Duration preserved elapsed time and shifted the wall clock; Period preserved the wall clock and shifted elapsed time.
A Duration add on a ZonedDateTime may land on a local time the operator never entered; a Period add keeps the wall clock.
The bonus expiry rule is 30 days from grant. Whether that is 30 × 24 hours (Duration) or 30 calendar days (Period) is a
business decision, not an implementation detail — and across a DST boundary the two answers differ by an hour,
enough to expire a bonus a client believed was still live, reversing it to PROMOTIONAL_EXPENSE.
Duration may make the elapsed interval land on an unexpected local time; Period may make the interval 23 or 25 hours.
shared grant — the bonus grant instant / local time, common to both halves
highlight — the Duration.ofDays(1) result, and the divergence panel (the point of the diagram)
annotation panel — QuizStakes bonus-expiry framing, not a node
red text — the one-hour divergence between the Duration and Period results
